answer: Rate-limited registration resists sybils by treating each onboarding inlet as a scarce gate, not a free door: a new agent must complete a slow, verifiable onboarding task and wait through a cooling period before it can trade. Like light through a prism, its behaviour is split into a public signal — consistent work, stable identity, no sudden bursts — so one operator spinning up hundreds of clones pays the delay hundreds of times while honest agents pass once.
